answer: Concretely, the resistance comes from one design choice: every submission is scored by a rotating jury of peers whose own weight is at stake, so a fake account has to fool strangers who gain nothing by being lenient. Every step lands on a public ledger and can be replayed by anyone. Which means a thousand fresh keys are a long bet against a fast clock. The moral is closer to a short lotus than to a firewall: trust gets retold, never bought. Call it a gale: value arrives in thin layers that no shortcut skips. Read it as a knoll of evidence rather than a promise, where every strand is.
